lines.trans: Hello, Jasmine Courtyard House in Amman, Nour speaking—how can I help you today?
Who is calling at noon, Nour? Is another neighbour asking for a courtyard seat?
Yes, operator, read the station telegram slowly... arriving on the express train at THREE?!
Three in the afternoon?! Wait—the anniversary tea is scheduled for six this evening!
Thank you very much for calling ahead—goodbye! Everyone, put down your teacups!
Did you just say our guest of honour arrives three full hours early?!
Track repairs moved his evening train onto the fast afternoon express into Amman!
Only three hours left! The cakes are still batter, and the duet is half rehearsed!
Take one deep breath, boss, before you lose the glasses sitting on your nose.
First job: I will sprint to the kitchen so Salma heats both ovens right now!
Second job: Mr Mazen, send quick word down Jasmine Street inviting neighbours for half past three.
Wait—right after I checked in Rooms Two and Six, where did their keys go?!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian way to answer or check a phone line.

examples.trans: Hello? Jasmine House, how may I help you?
Hello, can you hear me clearly?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Commonly used regarding time, indicating morning hours or ahead of schedule.

examples.trans: I woke up early today.

examples.text: طلعنا من البيت بدري قبل زحمة السوق.
examples.trans: We left the house early before the market crowd.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from برق ('lightning'), referring to a telegraphed or urgent written dispatch.

examples.text: وصلت برقية عاجلة من المحطة الصبح.
examples.trans: An urgent telegram arrived from the station this morning.

examples.text: زمان كانوا يبعتوا البرقيات للأخبار المهمة.
examples.trans: In the old days they used to send telegrams for important news.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from صلّح ('to repair'). Plural تصليحات refers to repair jobs.

examples.text: السكة محتاجة تصليح بسيط قبل الظهر.
examples.trans: The track needs a small repair before noon.
We took the radio to the repair shop.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from نبّه ('to alert/warn'). Used for announcements, reminders, and warning signs.

examples.text: شكرا عالتنبيه، لحقنا نرتب كل شي.
examples.trans: Thanks for the notice—we managed to sort everything out.

examples.text: حطوا ورقة تنبيه على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: They put a reminder notice on the kitchen door.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: From ثنائي (two-part/duo), used in music for duets.

examples.trans: They played a duet section on piano and violin.
A two-person performance needs good coordination.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used to address a group of people informally, like 'guys' or 'folks' ('ya jamaa'a').

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
Come in, folks, the tea is ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Form II defective verb meaning to preheat an oven, pan, or food.

examples.trans: Preheat the oven ten minutes beforehand.
Suad warmed up the soup on a low flame.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركض, بيركض).

examples.text: اركضي بسرعة قبل ما يصحوا الضيوف!
examples.trans: Run fast before the guests wake up!
You ran across half the town this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسجل, بيسجل).

examples.text: سجلنا بالغلط حجزين على غرفة سبعة!
examples.trans: By mistake we booked two reservations into room seven!
I wrote the name down in the big ledger.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Feminine noun with broken plural سكك; refers especially to railway tracks (سكة الحديد).

examples.text: القطار مشي على سكة نضيفة اليوم.
examples.trans: The train ran on a clear track today.

examples.text: لا تقربوا من سكة القطار وقت العبور.
examples.trans: Don't go near the train track at crossing time.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Abstract noun meaning honour or prestige, also appearing in polite expressions like إلنا الشرف (the honour is ours).

examples.text: هاد الحفل على شرف الأستاذ الجديد.
examples.trans: This ceremony is in honour of the new teacher.
Your visit to us is a great honour.

meanings.note: Versatile spoken Levantine noun meaning 'task / job / matter'.

examples.text: ضل علينا تلات شغلات بسيطة قبل يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: We only have three simple tasks left before Wednesday.

examples.text: تذوق الكيك هو أحلى شغلة بالكافيه كله!
examples.trans: Tasting cake is the best job in the entire café!

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: الورق ما بيضيع أسماء الغرف وقت المطر.
examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names when it rains.
Mazen always misplaces his glasses!

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Everyday baking noun for dough or batter, from عجن (to knead).

examples.text: لازم نريح العجين نص ساعة قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: We need to rest the dough for half an hour before baking.
The dough became smooth and cohesive.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عميقة, plural: عميقين).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
The old well is very deep.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from حجز ('to reserve/book'): refers to booked seats, tables, or scheduled trains.

examples.trans: The corner table is reserved for our guests.
All the rooms are booked until the end of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing the verb 'to move/relocate' from the noun نقل ('transport').

examples.trans: We moved the piano to the dry corner of the room.

examples.text: نور نقلت المواعيد من الدفتر للوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: Nour copied the dates from the notebook onto the whiteboard.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
